extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: A comprehensive multi-modal evaluation benchmark for MLLMs in video analysis with 900 videos and 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice questions spanning diverse domains, durations, and modalities.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed in three main steps: video collection from YouTube across a predefined domain hierarchy, question-answer annotation by recruited annotators, and a rigorous manual quality review including filtering with Gemini 1.5 Pro in a text-only setup.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The dataset includes 744 videos with subtitles out of 900 total videos; subtitles are only included if provided, while all 900 videos have audio.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos were sourced from YouTube, along with corresponding meta-information such as subtitles if provided and audio tracks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: QA pairs that could be answered solely from the text-only questions were filtered out using Gemini 1.5 Pro, and questions not meeting this criterion were returned to the original annotator for revision.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning thoroughly viewed each entire video and iteratively created three multiple-choice questions per video, each with four candidate options; each QA pair was then examined by a different annotator for clarity, answerability, logical consistency, and correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors performed statistical analysis showing Gemini 1.5 Pro achieved less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup after filtering, supporting that questions require video content; they also report a near-uniform option distribution to ensure unbiased evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators had strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset aims for relatively balanced distributions of video durations and unbiased answer-option distribution.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that long videos are more challenging due to a higher proportion of reasoning questions, sparse frame sampling in existing models, and difficulty in long-context understanding; it also notes that subtitle quality may affect results in the multilingual category.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as an evaluation benchmark for assessing MLLMs on video understanding tasks, including both image and video MLLMs and analyses with frames, subtitles, and audio.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce Video-MME , the first-ever full-spectrum, Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis.

description.evidence: In this paper, we introduce Video-MME , the first-ever full-spectrum, Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis. As exemplified in Figure 1, we meticulously curate a dataset of 900 videos across various scenarios, and annotate a set of 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice questions (3 per video) to foster a robust evaluation.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The construction of the Video-MME dataset involves three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Video Collection. To ensure comprehensive coverage across diverse video types, we first establish a domain hierarchy for sourcing raw videos from YouTube. Following the collection of raw video data, we annotate the videos with high-quality question-answer (QA) pairs.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: The resulting dataset consists of 900 videos, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audios, representing a range of domains with a relatively balanced distribution of video durations, as depicted on the right side of Figure 2.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Video Collection. To ensure comprehensive coverage across diverse video types, we first establish a domain hierarchy for sourcing raw videos from YouTube. Besides, we also obtain corresponding meta-information such as subtitles (if provided) and audios for in-depth investigation.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Furthermore, to ensure that the questions are sufficiently challenging enough and require video content as a critical clue to answer [72], we provide the text-only questions to Gemini 1.5 Pro and filter out QA pairs that can be answered solely based on the textual questions. Questions that do not meet this criterion are retumed to the original annotator for revision.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We employ a multiple-choice QA format to facilitate a straightforward and flexible assessment and recruit annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language leaming. Specifically, each annotator is tasked with thoroughly viewing the entire video, then iteratively creating three relevant questions, each accompanied by four candidate options, contributing to a total of 2,700 QA pairs. First, each QA pair undergoes examination by a different annotator to verify that (i) the language expression is clear and precise; (ii) the question is answerable with logically consistent candidate options, and the designated correct answer is appropriate.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Statistical analysis shows that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, underscoring the robustness of the video content-based requirement. In addition, the distribution of the options (A/B/C/D) follows a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring an unbiased evaluation.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Furthermore, to ensure that the questions are sufficiently challenging enough and require video content as a critical clue to answer [72], we provide the text-only questions to Gemini 1.5 Pro and filter out QA pairs that can be answered solely based on the textual questions.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: The resulting dataset consists of 900 videos, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audios, representing a range of domains with a relatively balanced distribution of video durations, as depicted on the right side of Figure 2. In addition, the distribution of the options (A/B/C/D) follows a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring an unbiased evaluation.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: As video duration increases, both open-sourced and commercial models exhibit a significant decline in performance. There are three main reasons for the performance decline. (1) Increased proportion of difficult tasks. (2) Increased sparsity in frame sampling, leading to a reduction in effective input information. (3) Increased difficulty in long context understanding. Multilingual can be regarded as an exception, possibly due to the quality of the subtitles.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: In this paper, we have introduced Video-MME, which is designed to evaluate MLLMs on video understanding tasks. The results also demonstrate that Video-MME is a universal benchmark that applies to both image and video MLLMs.
